terms: ## Conversational Texture The operator explicitly removed the per-milestone approval loop (proceed to DONE). This is material product code in packages/main, so it follows the repro-first discipline (a RED test proving the pack currently renders to a control-arm experiment task, and a throwaway SPIKE proving the shared gate suppresses it, before the dev story's implementation) and, because it changes lifecycle gate/surface behavior, expects the high-risk review-assurance floor (3x2 host quorum) at DONE. Genuine Claude single-host DEV + Codex host-2 adversarial review, the pattern that closed B-047f and B-337f.

## Key Insights The understanding workflow established the precise current state. (1) The arm switch that exists today is resolveHintMode(storyId) in packages/main/src/core/hint-mode.ts:21 (sha256 first-byte parity, even=on/odd=off, pure, per-STORY not per-experiment) consumed only by surfaceExperienceHints in packages/main/src/core/experience-hint-surface.ts:71-127, which ALWAYS computes the hints section + hintIds and render-gates a single ternary (renderedSection = hintMode==='on' ? section : '' at :125), firing experience_hint_surfaced on BOTH arms (:105-112) with the lossless would-have-hinted set. This is gated at exactly TWO sites: PLAN via handlers/story-review.ts:658 and REVIEW via handlers/transition-effects.ts:333. That both-arms-compute-and-log design IS the plan's Shadow C (there is no literal third arm; HintMode is only 'on'|'off'). (2) The RICHER surface, the runtime memory pack (buildMemoryFreshnessPack + renderMemoryFreshnessPack* + renderMemoryFreshnessPackSummary at playbook-runtime-memory.ts:439), is rendered UNGATED at every one of the 8 RuntimeConsumer entrypoints (the enum at playbook-runtime-memory.ts:44-52); the authoritative completeness oracle is the consumer-wiring list at handlers/playbook-runtime-memory.ts:110-118 used by playbook_runtime_health. renderMemoryRuntimePreflight is only a LOCAL session.ts helper (2 sites); the other 6 consumers render the pack directly, so there is no single existing choke point — M3 introduces one shared gate the render sites route through. (3) authority='non_authoritative'/gateEvidence=false are set at playbook-runtime-memory.ts:92-93/156/558/713 and must stay. (4) There is NO experimentId concept in the code today (grep zero hits for experiment-arm); the arm must, for experiment tasks, come from an out-of-band per-task signal the M6/M7 runner sets, cleanly falling back to today's behavior when absent so normal work is unchanged.

## Solution Tradeoffs Use an ENV-based per-task arm signal (PROOFBOUND_EXPERIMENT_ARM in {control,treatment} + PROOFBOUND_EXPERIMENT_ID) rather than a persisted per-story field: the M6/M7 runner assigns the arm per fixture-run (from the S1 pair ledger) and launches the host process with that env, and a null/absent env means normal non-experiment work that renders the pack exactly as today (the render-gate is a no-op outside experiments, verified byte-identical). resolveExperienceArm is a pure leaf (reads only the env object passed in, no fs/time/random) so it is trivially testable and mirrors resolveHintMode's purity discipline. The shared gate (gateRuntimeMemoryRender) centralizes compute-always / render-on-treatment-or-normal / suppress-on-control / log-on-both, so the 7-8 render sites each become a one-line delegation and the consumer-wiring completeness list doubles as the gate-coverage oracle. Control-arm retrieval blocking lives in command-policy.ts (the existing per-command gate) keyed on resolveExperienceArm()==='control', returning a clear refusal for the memory-retrieval command set; this is mechanical (not instruction-only) per plan S9. The event mirrors experience_hint_surfaced: runtime_memory_pack_surfaced with {experimentId, arm, consumer, packDigest, would-have-surfaced ids}, deduped per (experimentId, consumer, round) like the hints event. This story does NOT build the M6 runner, the M4 scorer, or touch S1/M1 fixtures — only the product-side switch.

## Trigger Event On 2026-07-03, after M1 (B-337f, the trap-fixture generator) merged to main (1b523cdfb, Proofbound CLI 0.3.143), the operator's standing order (execute the ablation-plan milestones in order to DONE) advances to M3, the product-code arm switch. A 4-reader understanding workflow (2026-07-03) mapped the exact gap this story closes.

Create packages/main/src/core/experience-arm.ts exporting resolveExperienceArm(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv | Record<string,string|undefined>): { experimentId: string; arm: 'control' | 'treatment' } | null — pure (reads only the passed env, no fs/git/time/random; mirrors hint-mode.ts purity). Returns the pair when PROOFBOUND_EXPERIMENT_ARM is exactly 'control' or 'treatment' AND PROOFBOUND_EXPERIMENT_ID is a non-empty slug; returns null otherwise (absent, malformed, or unknown arm value) so normal non-experiment work is unaffected. RED evidence (repro-first, per B-8628): add a failing check to a new smoke packages/main/src/tasks/experience-arm-gate-smoke.ts asserting that with PROOFBOUND_EXPERIMENT_ARM=control the shared pack gate (to be built in CHK-002) returns an empty render — this fails before CHK-002 exists (the gap: the pack renders regardless of arm). Unit-cover resolveExperienceArm: control/treatment accepted; absent/empty/unknown('shadow','on','')/missing-id -> null; env object is not mutated. Verify node dist smoke runs and npm test green.

Create the shared gate in packages/main/src/core/runtime-memory-arm-gate.ts: gateRuntimeMemoryPackRender(root, { consumer, pack, renderedLines, roundKey, env? }) -> string[] that (a) resolves the arm via resolveExperienceArm(env ?? process.env); (b) when null (normal work) returns renderedLines unchanged — byte-for-byte identical to today; (c) when arm='treatment' returns renderedLines AND, (d) when arm='control' returns [] (suppress); (e) in BOTH experiment arms, emits a runtime_memory_pack_surfaced activity event once per (experimentId, consumer, roundKey) — dedup via readActivityLogTail like experience-hint-surface.ts:96-101 — with {timestamp, event, experimentId, arm, consumer, packDigest (a stable sha256 of the would-have-surfaced pack top-hits), surfacedIds}; failures swallowed (try/catch, never throw, treat as pass-through render on error). Route ALL runtime-memory pack render sites through this gate: the session.ts renderMemoryRuntimePreflight helper (2 call sites) plus the direct render sites in handlers/lattice-handoff.ts, handlers/story-create.ts, handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts, handlers/done-closure.ts, handlers/done-prepare.ts, and the final_response_check path in handlers/playbook-runtime-memory.ts — the exact set enumerated by the consumer-wiring list at handlers/playbook-runtime-memory.ts:110-118. authority=non_authoritative/gateEvidence=false are untouched. Extend experience-arm-gate-smoke.ts: control -> [] + one event on both arms with matching packDigest and lossless surfacedIds; treatment -> full render + event; normal (no env) -> render byte-identical to a no-gate baseline and ZERO events; per-(experimentId,consumer,round) dedup. Update the playbook_runtime_health wiring oracle if the render-site signatures change so the drift check still passes. Verify npm test green.
Experience-ablation M3: gate the full runtime memory pack under an experiment arm + control-arm retrieval blocking
experience-layer

In packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts, add a check keyed on resolveExperienceArm(process.env)?.arm === 'control' that refuses the memory-RETRIEVAL command set — recall, dev_memory_start, dev_memory_preflight, playbook_diff/playbook_activate-class read paths, learning_scan, learning_effectiveness, memory_playbook_baseline_generate/verify, and any other command whose effect is to surface stored memory/playbooks/lessons to the host — with a clear refusal message ('blocked on the experiment control arm: memory retrieval is disabled to keep the control-arm isolation mechanical, plan S9'). Non-experiment and treatment-arm sessions are unaffected (the check is a no-op unless arm==='control'). Do NOT block memory-WRITE/audit commands that do not surface memory to the host (e.g. dev_memory_capture, playbook_outcome_record) unless they also read-and-surface. Extend the smoke: a control-arm env blocks a representative retrieval command (recall) and permits it on treatment/normal; the blocked set is enumerated and asserted. Verify node scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs still passes (if the command set is process-fact-registered) and npm test green.
M3
Mechanical control-arm retrieval blocking in command-policy

Milestone M3 of the experience-layer A/B ablation plan (product code, packages/main). Today the sha256-parity render-gate (resolveHintMode + surfaceExperienceHints) covers only the review-entrypoint experience HINTS at two sites; the richer runtime memory PACK (buildMemoryFreshnessPack/renderMemoryFreshnessPack*) is rendered UNGATED at all 8 RuntimeConsumer lifecycle entrypoints (session_brief, dev_memory_start, host_handoff, story_create, story_advance, done_prepare, done_closure, final_response_check). M3 extends the gate to the full pack under an EXPERIMENT ARM: (1) a pure env-based arm resolver (resolveExperienceArm) returning {experimentId, arm: control|treatment} from PROOFBOUND_EXPERIMENT_ARM/PROOFBOUND_EXPERIMENT_ID, or null when not an experiment task; (2) a shared gate that every pack render site routes through — ALWAYS build the pack, RENDER it on treatment (and on non-experiment normal work, preserving current behavior byte-for-byte), SUPPRESS the render on control, and LOG a runtime_memory_pack_surfaced event on BOTH arms with the lossless would-have-surfaced pack digest (the plan's Shadow C = both-arms-compute-and-log, mirroring the existing experience_hint_surfaced design); (3) mechanical control-arm retrieval blocking in command-policy so a control-arm host cannot pull memory via recall/dev_memory_*/playbook_*/learning_*/memory_playbook_* commands. Normal (non-experiment) sessions are unchanged. Memory stays authority=non_authoritative, gateEvidence=false. No change to the experiment fixtures/protocol/ledger (S1/M1); this is the product-side switch those artifacts drive.
